events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.95)
events.body:
The case is a no-show cancellation fee dispute: driver cancelled at 12:09:25 and a $6.61 cancellation fee was charged [F3][F6]. Under NS-0 the cancellation fee is only valid if the driver's no-show branch (NS-1) is met, since cancelled_by = driver [F3][NS-0].

NS-1(i) is met: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:06:15 [F5][NS-1]. But NS-1(ii) fails: at that moment GPS placed him 600 m from the pickup, and his closest approach across the whole wait was 599 m [F5][F1][NS-1]. The platform also never recorded an arrival at the pickup point [F4][NS-1]. NS-1(iii) fails as well: after the tap he spent 0 s within 200 m of the pickup [F5][NS-1], and his only stationary spell, 3 min 30 s, was spent 600 m away [F2][NS-1]. Time waited is only credited when it is waited at the pickup point, so the duration does not rescue him.

The driver's written statement that he waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup [F12] is a claim contradicted by the GPS and timeline records [F1][F2][F4][F5]; system records prevail over statements and NS-1 measures the wait by GPS, not by assertion [NS-1]. The rider's contemporaneous 12:07 message "I'm at the pickup point, no car here. Where are you?" [F9] matches the GPS gap and the chat record is complete and fully timestamped [F11][NS-1].

With NS-1(ii) and (iii) failing, NS-2 requires the $6.61 cancellation fee to be refunded in full [F3][F6][NS-2]. The amount is the cancellation fee stated on the fare record, $6.61 [F6][NS-2] — no per-km computation is needed because this is a fixed cancellation-fee item, not metered distance.

NS-2 further provides that where the driver confirmed arrival while GPS showed him outside the pickup range, the case carries a flag_account referral for abuse of the arrival/cancellation button [F5][F1][NS-2]; that flag is set via the structured field. RD-6 is not needed for this flag: the driver's profile shows 1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 days [F17], but profile facts may not decide the case, and NS-2's own abuse branch is the operative clause here [NS-2].

Safety screen: I read all three chat messages [F8][F9][F10], the complaint and the driver's statement [F12]. They contain a pickup coordination message, the rider's question about the driver's location, and the driver's cancellation notice — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; no safety concern arises [SAFE-1]. Evidence is sufficient: the GPS trace covers the wait to the cancellation without a hole, the timeline is complete, and the chat is fully timestamped [F5][F11][NS-1].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher, and refer the driver's account for review of the false "I'm Here" tap + flag_account

claims.assertion: The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:06:15 while 600 m from the pickup point, so NS-1(i)-(ii) fail: he was never at the pick-up location according to GPS and the platform never recorded him arriving there.
The driver's closest approach to the pickup point was 599 m at 12:06:55 and he never came within 200 m at any time, so he could not have waited for the rider at the designated location.

The driver's own GPS shows him stationary 12:05:55–12:09:25 (3 min 30 s) at a point 600 m from the pickup, and his time within 200 m after the tap is 0 s, so NS-1(iii) (continuous waiting at the pickup for more than 3 minutes) is not satisfied.

The rider messaged at 12:07 that she was at the pickup point with no car present, and the driver only replied at 12:09 that he had to cancel — consistent with the system records and contradicting the driver's written claim that the rider never showed up.
Because NS-1 (i), (ii) and (iii) all fail, the $6.61 cancellation fee charged to the rider (F6) must be refunded in full.

Since the driver pressed "I'm Here" while GPS placed him outside the pickup range (>200 m), the case also warrants a driver account flag for abuse of the arrival/cancellation button, supported by his 90-day record of 1 upheld no-show dispute.

weaknesses: The driver may argue he was stationary for 3 min 30 s before cancelling (F2) and that he pressed "I'm Here" (F5), so on his reading he did "wait"; the answer is that the wait was 600 m away from the pickup, which NS-1(ii)/(iii) requires to be at the pickup point.

The driver's written statement (F12) asserts he waited at the pickup for over 3 minutes; standing alone it supports his account, but it is contradicted by the gps facts F1/F2/F5, which the policy says prevail over statements, and by the rider's contemporaneous chat (F9).
The rider has a 4.4 rating and a thin 172-day history (F16), which the driver could use rhetorically, though profile facts cannot decide the case and she has 0 disputes in 90 days.

claims.assertion: The system records show the driver never reached the pickup point: his closest approach was 599 m (F1) and the platform never recorded an arrival (F4), so the $6.61 cancellation fee is not supported and must be refunded in full.

NS-1 (ii) fails because at the moment the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:06:15 he was 600 m from the pickup point, outside any credible arrival radius (F5); NS-2 therefore requires refund_full of the $6.61 fee (F3, F6).

NS-1 (iii) also fails: after the tap the driver accumulated 0 s within 200 m of the pickup (F5), and his only stationary period was 3 min 30 s spent 600 m away (F2), which is not waiting at the pickup point.

The rider's contemporaneous message at 12:07 ("I'm at the pickup point, no car here. Where are you?") (F9) matches the GPS record of a 600 m gap (F1, F2), confirming she was present and the driver was not; the chat record is complete and fully timestamped (F11).

The driver's own written statement that he "waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" (F12) is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records (F1, F4, F5), and under the system-record rule the GPS facts prevail; the rider's account, not the driver's, is the reliable one.

The driver tapped "I'm Here" while 600 m from the pickup point (F5), which the policy treats as abuse of the arrival/waiting button, and his 90-day history already contains one upheld no-show dispute (F17); a flag_account referral is warranted alongside the refund, while the rider has zero disputes (F16).

No traffic or weather excuse is available to the driver: no incidents were recorded near the route in the trip window (F14), and the only speed-band record, Jalan Besar band 3 at 20–29 km/h (F13), is not severe congestion (band 1–2); weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain (F15).

weaknesses: The driver is my client, and his own written statement (F12) squarely contradicts the GPS record (F1, F5): he asserts he waited at the pickup, which the track shows he never reached within 200 m — the judge will read this as a credibility problem, not merely a mistake.

The driver's 90-day profile already shows 1 upheld no-show dispute (F17), and the rider has a clean record (F16); the other side will use F17 both to attack his credibility and to support a flag_account referral.

The stationary period of 3 min 30 s (F2) superficially resembles a genuine wait, and the chat message "I'm here already" (F8) plus the three-minute wait then cancellation (F10) give the opposing side a narrative of a good-faith wait; only the 600 m GPS distance (F1, F2, F5) defeats it.

Agreed: at 12:06:15, the tap moment, GPS put the driver 600 m from the pickup (F5), so NS-1(ii) fails and NS-2 gives refund_full of the $6.61 on record (F3, F6).
Agreed: within-200 m time after the tap is 0 s (F5) and the only stationary spell was 3 min 30 s at 600 m (F2), so NS-1(iii) fails and the rider's client wins on the same ground.

Agreed: no RD-4 excuse exists — no incidents near the route in the trip window (F14), band 3 at 20–29 km/h (F13) is not severe congestion (band 1–2), and weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain (F15).

Conceded on the facts: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:06:15 while 600 m away (F5) and the platform never logged an arrival (F4), so NS-1(i)-(ii) cannot be met — my brief D1/D2 already argued the same and requests the same refund.
Accepted — the closest approach of 599 m (F1) confirms the 200 m arrival test was never met at any moment, which is precisely why the fee fails under NS-1 and NS-2.
Accepted — 0 s inside 200 m after the tap (F5) and the 3 min 30 s stationary period spent 600 m away (F2) mean NS-1(iii) fails; the duration is irrelevant when it was not spent at the pickup point.

Accepted — the rider's 12:07 message (F9) matches the GPS gap (F1, F4) while the driver's post-trip statement (F12) is contradicted by the system records, and the chat is complete and timestamped (F11).
Not contested on the outcome: NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) all fail (F1, F4, F5), so NS-2 gives refund_full of the $6.61 fee (F3, F6) — this is the identical amount I request in D2.

No objection to the flag being sent for Ryde's own review: the tap at 600 m (F5) falls within NS-2's abuse wording and the 90-day upheld no-show dispute (F17) supports it, but per RD-6 the profile entry is only an additional referral and the refund itself rests on the GPS facts, not on F17.
